Miami's top-rated ice cream shop
Feb 2023
What's the No. 1 ice cream shop in Miami, Florida? In my research, I couldn't find even one negative review of Azucar Ice Cream Factory. Located at 1503 Southwest 8th Street or the Calle Ocho in Miami's Little Havana neighborhood, it creates artisanal gourmet ice cream and sorbet in Cuban and tropical flavors. Founded in 2011, Azucar is open from 11 to 9 Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday, 11 to 11 on Thursday, Friday and Saturday and 11 to 10 on Sunday. "We like it sweet" is Azucar's motto and customers have an opportunity to test it while sampling a menu of flavors that boggle the mind. My wife and I were delighted with cinnamon ice cream with oatmeal cookies, vanilla ice cream with marshmallow swirls, peanut butter and Oreos, Ghirardelli chocolate brownies and chocolate chunk cookies in vanilla ice cream and banana ice cream, chocolate chunk and peanuts. But judge for yourself. Is Azucar as good as advertised? Signature flavors include Cuban coffee and Oreo, Guinness chocolate, coconut flan, caramel, Cuban vanilla, peanut butter and bananas, key lime pie and lemon basil. Classic flavors include vanilla, chocolate, strawberry, banana, cinnamon, lemon, pistachio, mango, almond and rum raisin. Sorbet flavors include passion fruit, watermelon mint, peach, coconut, mango, strawberry and lemon. It's a great way to cap off an exhausting day of sight-seeing. But how do you decide which flavor is best?

If you are in Miami this is a place not to be missed on Calle 8 in “Little Havana”. It offers a large selection of very different home made ice creams. They offer 24 different ice creams everyday. They do not sell the same flavors everyday and they also offer “Holiday” specific flavors like for Easter, Christmas, etc. Some of my favorites are: Abuela Maria, a mixture of cream cheese and guava paste, Plátano Maduro (sweet plantain), Cafe con Leche (Cuban coffee & Oreo), etc. They ale have chocolate and vanilla and many others “standard flavors. We went to dinner in Coconut Grove and drove to Calle Ocho for ice cream at Azúcar. Don’t miss the guayaberas made into cushions and covered with clear plastic like many of the Cubans used to preserve their cloth-covered soft cushioned furniture. A very clever idea using it for commercial purposes. 
“Azúcar” was the favorite phrase of the Cuban legend, Celia Cruz, the queen of salsa and arch-enemy of the Castro regime. Cruz's 1986 album, Ritmo En El Corazon, brought home her first career GRAMMY for “Best Tropical Latin Performance at the 32nd GRAMMY Awards.
The lobby of Azúcar has a large painting depicting Celia’s face and distinctive hair do.
Don’t waste any time to visit this place.
